disclaimer: Practice suggestions are educational, not psychological diagnoses or validated personality scores.

scenarios.title: A frustrated customer
scenarios.context: A customer says: 'I've explained this three times, and nobody is listening.'

options.text: I can see why repeating yourself is frustrating. Let me recap what I understand so far.
options.why: Acknowledges the impact and checks understanding.

options.text: Please calm down so I can help.
options.why: Can sound dismissive and escalates tension.

options.text: Our previous agents followed the process.
options.why: Defending the process does not address the customer's concern.

scenarios.title: An unrealistic request
scenarios.context: Your teammate asks you to complete their entire task while you have an urgent deadline.

options.text: I cannot take on the full task today, but I can help review the first part.
options.why: Sets a boundary while offering realistic help.

options.text: Fine, I'll do it, even if I miss my deadline.
options.why: Overcommitting creates preventable issues.

options.text: That's ridiculous. Do your own work.
options.why: Hostility makes collaboration harder.

scenarios.title: Two colleagues disagree
scenarios.context: Two teammates are disputing who owns a customer escalation.

options.text: Let's clarify the handoff rule and agree on next steps.
options.why: Focuses on shared process and resolution.

options.text: The more senior colleague must be right.
options.why: Seniority is not evidence of ownership.

options.text: Ignore it and wait for someone else.
options.why: Avoidance can leave the customer case unresolved.

scenarios.title: Giving developmental feedback
scenarios.context: An agent repeatedly skips summarizing customer requests.

options.text: On the last two calls, the request wasn't recapped. Let's practise a 15-second summary.
options.why: Specific evidence plus a practice action supports improvement.

options.text: You're bad at listening.
options.why: Labels a person instead of describing behavior.

options.text: Your score was low. Fix it.
options.why: It lacks an actionable improvement step.

scenarios.title: A teammate is behind
scenarios.context: A teammate asks for help when your own queue is busy.

options.text: I have two urgent cases. Can we prioritize and involve the team lead if needed?
options.why: Balances competing responsibilities and collaboration.

options.text: I'll take everything without checking priorities.
options.why: Unplanned workload transfers create risk.

options.text: Not my problem.
options.why: Dismisses a chance to coordinate.

scenarios.title: An unclear request
scenarios.context: A caller mentions a charge, an address change and a promised callback.

options.text: Let me confirm the three issues and which one is most urgent.
options.why: Summarizes and clarifies priority.

options.text: We'll only discuss the charge.
options.why: Ignores the broader request.

options.text: I know what you mean.
options.why: Assumes understanding without verifying.

scenarios.title: A delayed update
scenarios.context: A promised customer update is late because another team has not responded.

options.text: I'm sorry the update is late. I'm checking the status and will share the next confirmed step.
options.why: Takes ownership without an unsupported guarantee.

options.text: It's the other team's fault.
options.why: Blame is unhelpful to the customer.

options.text: We'll definitely resolve it in ten minutes.
options.why: Inventing timelines can damage trust.

scenarios.title: A difficult call ends
scenarios.context: After a hostile call, you feel frustrated and the next caller is waiting.

options.text: Use an approved brief reset and approach the next caller without carrying over frustration.
options.why: A short regulated transition helps maintain professionalism.

options.text: Take the frustration out on the next caller.
options.why: Transfers harm to another person.

options.text: Ignore procedures and leave the queue indefinitely.
options.why: Abandoning process may create further problems.

scenarios.title: Different communication needs
scenarios.context: A customer asks you to explain the process more slowly.

options.text: Of course. I'll take it one step at a time and pause for questions.
options.why: Adapts respectfully to the customer's request.

options.text: The instructions are already simple.
options.why: Dismisses an access need.

options.text: Ask someone else.
options.why: Unnecessarily deflects assistance.

scenarios.title: Competing team priorities
scenarios.context: You and another colleague need the same limited meeting slot.

options.text: Can we compare deadlines and find a time or format that meets both needs?
options.why: Explores interests and mutually workable alternatives.

options.text: I booked it first, end of discussion.
options.why: Focuses on position rather than options.

options.text: I'll agree to anything and not mention my deadline.
options.why: Concealing constraints leads to poor agreements.
